## Architecture Decisions (Why This Structure)

| Layer | Responsibility | Reuse Boundary |
|-------|---------------|----------------|
| `shared/core/` | Engine loop, input, pooling | Game-agnostic; every game imports these |
| `shared/vfx/` | All 6 required VFX systems | Game-agnostic; games call `emit()`/`shake()`/`trigger()` |
| `shared/graphics/` | Post-processing, procedural assets | Shared bloom config, texture generators |
| `shared/audio/` | Synthesized sound | Shared SFX presets, music engine |
| `shared/math/` | Pure functions | Zero side effects, no game knowledge |
| `[GameName]/` | Game-specific logic | Isolated; only imports from `shared/` |

### Memory Ownership Model
- **GameEngine** owns the renderer, scene, camera, composer. Disposes all on `destroy()`.
- **ObjectPool** owns pooled instances. Game code borrows via `acquire()`, returns via `release()`.
- **ParticleManager** owns the InstancedMesh and its dummy objects. Hard-cap enforced at construction.
- **MotionTrails** owns ghost meshes. Auto-cleans when entities die.
- Every `Material`, `Geometry`, `Texture` created in `shared/` is tracked and disposed when the engine shuts down.

### Fixed-Timestep Loop
```
accumulator += realDelta
while (accumulator >= fixedDt) {
    accumulator -= fixedDt
    update(fixedDt * hitStopTimescale)
}
render(interpolationAlpha)
```
This decouples physics from frame rate and gives HitStop a clean integration point.

---

## Compliance Statements

**Anti-Lazy Directive:** Every function will be fully implemented. No `// ...`, no placeholders, no TODOs. If a file is too long for one response, I will stop mid-file and resume on "continue" from the exact character.

**Strict Memory Management:** Every `Geometry`, `Material`, and `Texture` will have a corresponding `.dispose()` call in the destruction path. Object pools prevent GC churn. The ParticleManager enforces its 500-particle cap at the API level.

**Sequential Output Protocol:** I will not generate any game code until you name the game and approve the plan. The `shared/` layer will be written first, then the game-specific code, in dependency order.
